guides.title: Use the Deno fetch adapter and its asset binding
guides.summary: Compose the runtime-neutral application with Deno's fetch adapter, understand binding precedence, and dispose process-local WebSocket resources.
guides.markdown:
# Use the Deno adapter

Create one `createDenoAdapter` instance for the process and pass it to `createApp({ runtimeAdapter })`. Export a fetch handler that calls `runtime.fetch(app, request, env)`, or use `runtime.serve(app)` for local `Deno.serve()`. The adapter injects `ASSETS.fetch`; configured `options.env` values are merged first and request bindings override matching names.

Deno WebSocket instances are process-local. `maxInstances` includes pending initializations, and `idleTimeoutMs` is enforced during socket activity rather than by a background timer. This adapter does not provide durable `stateful: true` WebSocket pages; persist application data in a database or deploy with Cloudflare Durable Objects.

Await `runtime.dispose()` when an embedded host stops using it. `runtime.serve(app)` also disposes on `server.shutdown()` or when `server.finished` settles. Cleanup waits for active actions, so application actions must settle. Standalone entries explicitly call `installDenoShutdown(server, { onComplete })` inside `import.meta.main` to own SIGTERM/SIGINT. Both signals share one graceful shutdown with a default 10-second deadline; unfinished HTTP connections are aborted at the deadline. The completion result reports `forced`, `cleanupCompleted`, and `cleanupFailed`. Use the completion hook to choose process exit status; the helper itself never exits. Imports install no signal listeners. Embedded hosts may uninstall ownership or call shutdown explicitly. Ignored external I/O is not claimed complete or rolled back.

The optional Vite development integration is imported from `/vite`; its supervisor uses local authenticated loopback channels and is not a security sandbox.
